1. When player is at (30, 11) and presses UP, blocks move up and player moves to (24, 11)
2. When player is at (24, 11) and presses UP, blocks move up and player moves to (18, 11)
3. When player is at (18, 11) and presses UP, blocks move up and player moves to (12, 11)
4. When player is at (12, 11) and presses LEFT/RIGHT/ACTION7, blocks move left/right
So the player has different "modes":
- At (30, 11), (24, 11), (18, 11): UP moves blocks up and player up
- At (12, 11): LEFT/RIGHT/ACTION7 move blocks left/right
The key insight is that when blocks are in different rows and move UP, they can reorder. Looking at transition 10:
Before: [('R', (13, 42)), ('b', (19, 42)), ('N', (25, 36))]
After: [('R', (13, 42)), ('N', (19, 36)), ('b', (19, 42))]
The N and b blocks swapped positions when they moved up. This suggests that the order of blocks depends on their column positions when they move up.
Current state: blocks at [(N, 13, 18), (b, 13, 24), (R, 13, 30)], player at (30, 11)
Goal: reorder to [R, N, b] (matching HUD: red, green, blue)
To reorder the blocks, I need to:
1. Move blocks to different rows (using UP)
2. Move blocks to different columns (using LEFT/RIGHT)
3. Move blocks back to the same row (using UP or DOWN)
Let me think about the mechanics more carefully. When blocks move UP, they seem to move by 6 rows. When blocks are in the same row and move UP, they stay in the same row relative to each other. When blocks are in different rows and move UP, they might stack in a different order.
Actually, looking at transition 16:
Before: [('R', (13, 42)), ('N', (19, 18)), ('b', (19, 24))]
After: [('N', (13, 18)), ('b', (13, 24)), ('R', (13, 42))]

So the rule seems to be: when blocks move UP, they all move to the topmost available row, and their order is determined by their column positions (left to right).
Current state: [(N, 13, 18), (b, 13, 24), (R, 13, 30)]
If I move them left/right to change their column order, then move them up, they should reorder based on the new column positions.
To get [R, N, b], I need the column order to be R < N < b. Currently it's N < b < R (columns 18, 24, 30).
So I need to move R to the leftmost position, then N, then b.
But wait, the blocks move as a group when I press LEFT/RIGHT. So I can't move individual blocks. Let me think about this differently.
Actually, looking at the transitions more carefully, when blocks are in different rows, LEFT/RIGHT only affects the blocks in the same row as the player's horizontal path. Let me check this.
Transition 9: player at (24, 11), blocks [('R', (13, 42)), ('b', (19, 42)), ('N', (25, 42))]
After LEFT: [('R', (13, 42)), ('b', (19, 42)), ('N', (25, 36))]
Only the N block moved left! This suggests that LEFT/RIGHT only affects the block in the same row as the player's horizontal path.
So the mechanic is:
- UP: moves all blocks up by 6 rows
- LEFT/RIGHT: moves only the block(s) in the same row as the player's horizontal path
This means I can move individual blocks left/right by positioning the player at the same row as the block I want to move.
Current state: player at (30, 11), blocks at [(N, 13, 18), (b, 13, 24), (R, 13, 30)]
All blocks are in row 13. The player is at row 30. The player's horizontal path is at row 30 (based on the gray tiles).
To move individual blocks, I need to:
1. Move the player to the same row as the block I want to move
2. Use LEFT/RIGHT to move that block
But the player can only be at certain rows: 12, 18, 24, 30 (based on the transitions). The blocks are at row 13. So I can't position the player at row 13.
Wait, let me reconsider. Looking at the transitions, when the player is at (12, 11), LEFT/RIGHT moves all blocks. When the player is at (18, 11), LEFT/RIGHT moves only the blocks at row 19. When the player is at (24, 11), LEFT/RIGHT moves only the blocks at row 25.
So the player's horizontal path is at row = player_row + 6 (approximately). Let me check:
- Player at (12, 11): path at row 13 (blocks at row 13 moved)
- Player at (18, 11): path at row 19 (blocks at row 19 moved)
- Player at (24, 11): path at row 25 (blocks at row 25 moved)
- Player at (30, 11): path at row 31 (no blocks at row 31)
So the horizontal path is at row = player_row + 1. This means:
- Player at (12, 11): path at row 13
- Player at (18, 11): path at row 19
- Player at (24, 11): path at row 25
- Player at (30, 11): path at row 31
Current state: player at (30, 11), path at row 31, blocks at row 13.
To move the blocks at row 13, I need the player at row 12 (path at row 13).
Let me move the player up to row 12, then use LEFT/RIGHT to move the blocks.
